ME 101.name: Fundamentals of Mechanical Engineering
ME 101.description: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering. Analysis of real engineering problems using mechanical engineering principles.

ME 102.name: Introduction to Systems Engineering
ME 102.description: Treatment of engineering problems from a systems perspective and a unified application of mechanical engineering principles, introduction to and use of CAD systems and group projects.

ME 103.name: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design
ME 103.description: Introduction to Computer-Aided Design and SolidWorks, part modeling, features, and tolerancing; assembly modeling; engineering drawings and animation.

ME 211.name: Thermo-Fluids Engineering I
ME 211.description: First law of thermodynamics, first law in differential form, thermal resistance approach for heat transfer, fundamentals of fluid mechanics, thermodynamic properties, open systems, thermodynamic cycles, second law, refrigeration, heat pump, power cycles.

ME 212.name: Thermo-Fluids Engineering II
ME 212.description: Differential analysis of fluid flow, laminar and turbulent flow, head loss, boundary layer, drag and lift, conductive heat transfer, forced and natural convection, heat exchangers, radiative heat transfer.

ME 231.name: Mechanics and Materials I
ME 231.description: Introduction to statics, average stress and strain, linear elasticity, axial loading, torsion, bending, deflection of beams and shafts, transverse shear stress, combined loadings, energy methods.

ME 232.name: Mechanics and Materials II
ME 232.description: Three-dimensional stress and strain, stress and strain transformation, failure criteria, stress-strain curve, plasticity, fracture of cracked members, fatigue crack growth, stress- and strain-based approach to fatigue.

ME 299.name: Summer Practice I
ME 299.description: A minimum of four weeks summer practice in a manufacturing organization; observation of organization in its original settings; written report.

ME 341.name: Dynamics and Control I
ME 341.description: Modeling and control of dynamical systems. Particles, groups of particles and motion of solids, effects of forces, kinematics, Lagrange equations. Solutions in time and frequency domains.

ME 342.name: Dynamics and Control II
ME 342.description: Parametric modeling of systems and their analysis and control. Linear system theory, Laplace Transforms, transfer functions, introduction to feedback controls, root-locus analysis.

ME 343.name: Mechanical Vibrations
ME 343.description: Free and forced vibrations of single- and multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Fundamentals of modal analysis, damping and vibration control methods. Vibration measurement and analysis.

ME 361.name: Numerical Methods for Engineers
ME 361.description: Taylor series and approximation errors, solving systems of linear and nonlinear equations, curve fitting and interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, applications to systems of ordinary differential equations.
ME 361.prerequisite: (CS 114 or CS 115) and (MATH 220 or MATH 241 or MATH 224) and (MATH 240 or MATH 242)

ME 362.name: Finite Elements
ME 362.description: Solving partial differential equations of mechanics numerically. Fundamentals of the finite element method including weak form, shape functions, isoparametric approximation, Gauss quadrature, element types, assembly operation, sparsity pattern with application to 2D problems. Self-written finite element code in MATLAB. Computationa simulations of elastic materials and stress analysis using the MATLAB code. Domain discretization, pre-processing and post-processing aspects.

ME 371.name: Measurement and Instrumentation
ME 371.description: Principles of measurement and measurement systems, basic principles of signals and frequency domain representation, Fourier transform, mechanical modeling of measurement systems, probabilistic and statistical methods for measurement data analysis, measurement uncertainty calculation, basics of experiment design, measurement, recording and analysis of force, strain, temperature, humidity, flow, velocity, vibration and acceleration. Use of typical laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, frequency analyzers, operational amplifiers, and thermocouples.

ME 381.name: Design and Manufacturing
ME 381.description: Engineering materials, bulk deformation processes, material removal processes and machines, sintering, polymeric materials processes, additive manufacturing, economic and quality considerations, design principles, machine elements.

ME 384.name: Mechatronic Systems
ME 384.description: Introduction to analog electronics, semiconductor electronics, operational amplifiers and analog signal processing, digital electronics, microcontrollers, actuators, sensors, data acquisition, systems integration.
ME 384.prerequisite: PHYS 102 and (MATH 225 or MATH 240 or MATH 242) and (CS 114 or CS 115)

ME 399.name: Summer Practice II
ME 399.description: A minimum of four weeks summer practice in an engineering company; formulation of an ME problem and proposal for solutions to it; written report.
ME 399.prerequisite: ME 212 and ME 342 and ME 371 and ME 381

ME 401.name: Acoustics and Noise Control
ME 401.description: Fundamentals of generation and radiation of sounds. Sources of noise and control methods. Sound and vibration measurement and analysis.

ME 405.name: Machine Learning for Mechanical Engineering
ME 405.description: Statistics in Python, data management, visualization, regression and classification models, feature engineering, usage of databases, supervised and unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, active learning, Bayesian optimization, Gaussian process, decision trees and forests, neural networks, convolutional neural networks for mechanical engineering applications (e.g. microscopy image analysis, material structure-property relationship), atomistic descriptors, machine learning potentials for molecular dynamics, self-driving lab.
ME 405.prerequisite: (MATH 220 or MATH 224 or MATH 225 or MATH 241) and (MATH 230 or MATH 255 or MATH 260) and (CS 102 or CS 114 or CS 115) and (CHEM 201 or PHYS 212)

ME 412.name: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
ME 412.description: Finite volume methods (FVM) as a means of solving different type of differential equations that arise in fluid dynamics. Fundamentals of numerical analysis, ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations related to fluid mechanics and heat transfer. Error control and stability considerations. Numerical solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations.

ME 413.name: Biological Fluid Dynamics
ME 413.description: Application of fluid dynamics principles to internal (physiological) and external fluid flows in biological systems. The internal flows involve blood flow in veins and arteries, flows of blood cells, respiratory flows, ciliary flows. Examples for the external flows are flying of birds and insects, swimming micro-organisms such as bacteria, their collective behavior and synchronization (fish schools, bird flocks). Focusing on integrating fluid dynamics concepts to address various problems in biological systems. It primarily aims at developing a broad knowledge and a critical thinking regarding the current research challenges in biological fluid dynamics.
ME 413.prerequisite: CS 115 and MATH 220 and MATH 240 and ME 212

ME 418.name: Data-Based Control Systems
ME 418.description: Data Acquisition and Pre processing, System Identification, Reduced Order Modeling and Decomposition, Optimization Based Control, Learning Based Control.

ME 430.name: Heat Exchanger Design
ME 430.description: Principles of design, manufacture, and use of major types of heat exchangers. Applications of thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics laws, and empirical relations for common heat exchangers including boilers, condensers, evaporators, and cooling towers.

ME 431.name: Industrial Fluid Power
ME 431.description: Basic principles, introduction to hydraulic and pneumatic power systems. Hydraulic power systems: hydraulic fluids; distribution system; energy input and transfer devices; energy modulation devices; energy output and transfer devices; other components such as reservoirs, filters, and accumulators; system design and circuit analysis. Pneumatic power systems. Case studies.

ME 432.name: Applied Thermodynamics
ME 432.description: Design and analysis of devices and thermal processes using principles of thermodynamics. Examples include nuclear power stations, jet engines, energy conversion, internal combustion engines, desaliniation and others.

ME 434.name: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
ME 434.description: Classical thermodynamics, including the TdS equations and the Maxwell relations; development of thermodynamic property relations, behavior of real gases, thermodynamics of mixtures, phase equilibrium and chemical reactions and equilibrium with an emphasis on combustion reactions; statistical thermodynamics including the effect of molecular and atomic structure, statistical concepts and distributions, calculation of thermodynamic properties of gas-phase atoms and molecules, kinetic theory of gases, and vibrations in crystals and the electron gas in metals; selected applications.

ME 436.name: Renewable Energy Systems
ME 436.description: Principles of energy conversion among different states of energy including heat, electricity and optical energy. Direct energy conversion devices for thermic, thermo-ionic, magnetohydrodynamic, photovoltaic energy. Principles and theories of chemical and mechanical energy storage devices.

ME 438.name: Advanced Heat Transfer
ME 438.description: A comprehensive study of conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer in engineering systems. Conduction topics include multidimensional steady and transient analysis, finned surfaces, and shape factors. Convection covers boundary layers, internal and external flows, and developing flow in ducts for both laminar and turbulent regimes. Radiation topics include fundamental laws, directional and spectral property variations, view factors, and radiative exchange between surfaces.

ME 440.name: Automotive Engineering
ME 440.description: Automotive components. Modeling of vehicle dynamics. Maximum speed and acceleration calculations. Wheels and tires. Brake systems and performance. Suspension system and geometry. Steering system and geometry. Aerodynamics drag and effects on vehicle performance.

ME 442.name: Machinery Dynamics
ME 442.description: Introduction to the synthesis and analysis of linkages, cams and gear trains. Degree of freedom analysis of mechanisms. Kinematic analysis of mechanisms (position, velocity and acceleration). Graphical and analytical synthesis of mechanisms. Quasi-static and dynamic force analysis of mechanisms. Cams and gear trains.

ME 443.name: Machine Elements
ME 443.description: Stress analysis in 3-D. Stress concentration, factor of safety. Static design criteria; theories of failure for ductile and brittle materials. Fatigue design criteria under mean and combined stresses. Design of shafts. Design of permanent joints; riveted joints, welded joints. Design of bolted joints. Design of springs. Power transmission. Kinematics of gear drives; spur gears, helical gears, bevel gears, worm gears. Design of spur and helical gears. Friction, wear and lubrication. Design of sliding bearings. Selection of rolling element bearings. Design of couplings, clutches and brakes. Design of belt drives; flat belts, V-belts.

ME 446.name: Applications of Solid Mechanics
ME 446.description: Mathematical preliminaries, strain and compatibility, stress and equilibrium, displacement- and stress-based solutions of boundary value problems in isotropic linear elasticity, miscellaneous topics.

ME 453.name: Principles of Turbomachinery
ME 453.description: This course introduces the topic of turbomachinery to undergraduate students. In particular the course allows for a smooth transition from the study of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer to the subject of turbomachinery. More in general, it provides information on several types of turbomachines rather than concentrating specifically on one type by combining theory and applications to show how gas turbines, pumps and compressor function. Finally the course relates turbomachines to areas such as wind power and three-dimensional effects in axial turbomachines.

ME 455.name: Cellular Biomechanics
ME 455.description: Fundamental concepts and experimental techniques in molecular biology, statistical mechanics of polymers, review of solid and fluid mechanics. Mechanics of cellular polymers. Polymer networks and cytoskeleton. The role of stress in cytoskeleton dynamics as related to cell growth, spreading, motility and adhesion. Cellular mechanotransduction. Current research topics in cellular biomechanics.

ME 457.name: Metal Cutting Principles
ME 457.description: The basic principles of metal cutting. The mechanics of metal cutting, heat generation during metal cutting, modern cutting materials, tool life and tool wear, cutting fluids, surface roughness generated by cutting actions, chip control, economics of cutting, chatter vibration, abrasive machining and non-conventional machining processes.

ME 464.name: Topics in Modern Dynamics
ME 464.description: Phase Space, Equilibrium and Stability, Geometric Dynamics, Analytical Dynamics, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos, Coupled Oscillators and Synchronization, Neurodynamics, Economic Dynamics: Game Theory, Network Dynamics, Evolutionary Dynamics, Dynamics of Microswimmer Robots, Dynamics of Computer Games: Physics Engine.

ME 471.name: Advanced System Modeling
ME 471.description: Modeling of linear and nonlinear dynamical systems that have components from mechanical, electrical, chemical, thermal and fluidic domains. State space models, interaction between domains, time and frequency domain analysis. Control system design using root locus and bode plots.

ME 473.name: Flexible Robotics
ME 473.description: Design and manufacturing of flexible mechanisms. Biomechanics and bioinspiration. Kinematics and dynamics of robots and mechanisms. Mechanics and the effects of compliance on robot dynamics. Design optimization and system identification for flexible robots. Experimental validation of flexible robots.

ME 474.name: Mobile Robots
ME 474.description: An introductory course on mobile robotics fundamentals. Legged and wheel locomotion basics. Kinematic models, mobile robot maneuverability, holonomicity, and motion control of mobile robots. Perception in mobile robots. Localization of mobile robots. Path planning and obstacle avoidance strategies.

ME 480.name: Introduction to MEMS and Micro Systems
ME 480.description: Analysis of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), design of microsystems, components of MEMS devices such as beams, folded suspensions and their analysis; design metrics, beams as micromechanical springs, clean room fabrication techniques, MEMS sensors, accelerometers, gyroscopes, resonant mass/force sensors, MEMS actuation methods, measurement and noise analysis of MEMS devices.

ME 481.name: Mechanical Engineering Design I
ME 481.description: Development of a mechanical engineering project, design procedures, design selection, engineering statement of customer preferences, ethical and professional responsibilities of engineers. Projects lead to products.
ME 481.prerequisite: ENG 401 and ME 212 and ME 232 and ME 342 and ME 371 and ME 381

ME 482.name: Mechanical Engineering Design II
ME 482.description: Group project stressing the mechanical engineering design principles. Projects spanning from conceptual development to working products. Reports explaining the projects, design steps, analyses complemented by oral presentations.

ME 485.name: Design Project I
ME 485.description: Development of a mechanical engineering project, preliminary, thermofluidic and mechanical design procedures, design selection, ethical and professional responsibilities of engineers. Projects lead to products. Prerequisite(s): (ME212, ME341, ME371, ME381) and (ENG400 or ENG 401)
ME 485.prerequisite: ENG 401 and ME 212 and ME 232 and ME 341 and ME 381 and ME 384

ME 486.name: Design Project II
ME 486.description: Development of a mechanical engineering project, control system and mechatronic design procedures, manufacturing of a prototype, prototype testing, reports explaining the projects, design steps, analyses complemented by oral presentations. Prerequisite(s): ME342, ME384, ME485

ME 488.name: Systems Engineering and Product Development
ME 488.description: An introductory understanding of Development Stages for atypical product development cycle. Basic System Engineering Techniques and Approaches. Concepts such as reliability, maintainability, supportability, usability, manufacturability and affordibility. Codes and Standards. Technical Data Package and Configuration Management. Test Planning. Mass Affordability Production. Risk Assessment Techniques.

ME 489.name: Fundamentals of Design for Reliability
ME 489.description: Comprehensive definition of reliability. Introduction to reliability engineering, its basic definitions, applications and benefits. Confidence intervals and levels. Concept of target reliability. Case histories from aerospace, military, process control and power systems applications. Basic statistical and analytical functions and distribution types used by reliability engineers. Reliability analysis during the design phase. Qualification tests for components and assemblies. Interfaces of reliability, maintainability and risk engineering. Design guidelines for reliability, maintainability and quality. Statistical reliability testing. Reliability during the production phase. Standards about aerospace, defense and nuclear engineering. System reviews and related checklists. Construction of fault trees and fault tree analysis. Design of reliability testing. Failure causes and types. Effects of environmental conditions, age, mission time and stress. Mission profile and requirements. Failure modes, effects and criticality analysis and two different methods supported by examples. Ageing testing methods. Role of reliability departments in engineering organizations and systems projects.

ME 490.name: Undergraduate Research in ME
ME 490.description: Introduction to research techniques in mechanical engineering. Independent study on a research topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Documentation of the results for evaluation by the supervisor.

ME 501.name: Mathematical Techniques in Mechanical Engineering
ME 501.description: Ordinary differential equations and introduction to partial differential equations, series solutions, Fourier, Bessel and Legrendre functions, boundary value problems and eigenfunction expansions; calculus of variations. Classical partial differential equations related to mathematical physics, including Laplace transformation and the method of separation of variables.

ME 503.name: Numerical Methods in Mechanical Engineering
ME 503.description: Review of curve fitting, numerical differentiation and integration; numerical solutions of ordinary differential equations with Runge-Kutta and multi-step methods, boundary-value problems; numerical solutions of parabolic, elliptic and hyperbolic partial differential equations with applications.

ME 505.name: Machine Learning for Mechanical Engineering
ME 505.description: Statistics in Python, data management, visualization, regression and classification models, feature engineering, usage of databases, supervised and unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, active learning, Bayesian optimization, Gaussian process, decision trees and forests, neural networks, convolutional neural networks for mechanical engineering applications (e.g. microscopy image analysis, material structure-property relationship), atomistic descriptors, machine learning potentials for molecular dynamics, self-driving lab.

ME 511.name: Fluid Mechanics
ME 511.description: Development and application of control volume forms of mass, momentum and energy conservation laws, differential forms of these laws in Eulerian and Lagrangian coordinates, and Navier-Stokes equations. Applications to problems in incompressible and compressible laminar flows, boundary layers, hydrodynamic lubrication, transient and periodic flows, thermal boundary layers, convective heat transfer, and aerodynamic heating.

ME 513.name: Biological Fluid Dynamics
ME 513.description: Application of fluid dynamics principles to internal (physiological) and external fluid flows in biological systems. The internal flows involve blood flow in veins and arteries, flows of blood cells, respiratory flows, ciliary flows. Examples for the external flows are flying of birds and insects, swimming micro-organisms such as bacteria, their collective behavior and synchronization (fish schools, bird flocks). Focusing on integrating fluid dynamics concepts to address various problems in biological systems. It primarily aims at developing a broad knowledge and a critical thinking regarding the current research challenges in biological fluid dynamics.

ME 516.name: Tribology : Friction, Lubrication and Wear
ME 516.description: Introduction to the field of tribology. Fundamental principles of friction, lubrication, and wear from a mechanical engineering point of view. Surface roughness, contact between surfaces, adhesion, macroscopic laws of friction, fluid film lubrication, boundary lubrication, wear mechanisms, nanotribology.

ME 518.name: Data-Based Control Systems
ME 518.description: Data Acquisition and Pre processing, System Identification, Reduced Order Modeling and Decomposition, Optimization Based Control, Learning Based Control.

ME 519.name: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
ME 519.description: Covers the modern aspects of dynamical systems, especially nonlinear systems and the chaos. Phase space representation of dynamical systems, Bifurcations, Dynamics of 1D and 2D systems, and Limit Cycles are covered. Coupled Oscillators, Synchronization, Network Dynamics and Disease Spread will be studied as relevant applications. Finally, topics on chaos are covered which includes the Lorenz Equation, 1D maps, Fractals and Strange Attractors.

ME 523.name: Molecular Simulation of Materials
ME 523.description: Review of continuum field theories, atomistic potentials, molecular statics, discrete-to-continuum transition, finite element implementation, calculation of various material properties.

ME 525.name: Introduction to Nanomechanics
ME 525.description: Linear atomic chains, lattice vibrations in 2D and 3D. Properties of phonon gas. Elasticity relations. Piezoelectricity. Static and dynamic deformations of solids. Accelerometers, gyroscopes and resonant mechanical sensors. Nanomechanical measurement techniques, dissipation and nonlinearity in nanomechanics.

ME 534.name: Advanced Engineering Thermodynamics
ME 534.description: Classical thermodynamics, including the TdS equations and the Maxwell relations; development of thermodynamic property relations, behavior of real gases, thermodynamics of mixtures, phase equilibrium and chemical reactions and equilibrium with an emphasis on combustion reactions; statistical thermodynamics including the effect of molecular and atomic structure, statistical concepts and distributions, calculation of thermodynamic properties of gas-phase atoms and molecules, kinetic theory of gases, and vibrations in crystals and the electron gas in metals; selected applications.

ME 543.name: Sound and Vibration
ME 543.description: Forced and free oscillations, frequency and impulse response of mechanical systems. Wave propagation in solids and fluids. Interaction of waves with boundaries, transmission, reflection, and absorption. Radiation and scattering of sound and interference. Waveguides and cavities. Wave propagation in periodic structures.

ME 546.name: Applications of Solid Mechanics
ME 546.description: Mathematical preliminaries, strain and compatibility, stress and equilibrium, displacement- and stress-based solutions of boundary value problems in isotropic linear elasticity, miscellaneous topics.

ME 550.name: Continuum Mechanics
ME 550.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts and tools for mechanics. Overview of tensor calculus, the kinematics of deformation, concepts of stress, strain, linearization, objectivity and the balance laws for mass, momentum and energy. Materials modeling aspects such as constitutive laws and material symmetry applications to solid and fluid mechanics.

ME 552.name: The Finite Element Method
ME 552.description: Numerical solution of partial differential equations describing engineering problems. Fundamentals of the finite element methods including the weighted residual method, shape functions, numerical integration, assembly and error analysis by solving 1D linear second order elliptic equations technique and extension to 2D and 3D elliptic problems. Fourth order equations, time-dependent parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations and non-linear problems. Applications problems in applied mechanics, elasticity, vibrations, heat conduction, and others. Background required in calculus, linear algebra and differential equations.

ME 554.name: Mechanics of Composite Materials
ME 554.description: Introduction to metallic, ceramic and polymeric composites and their manufacturing. Microstructural descriptors for unidirectional, short-fiber and particular composites. Macro- and micromechanical analysis. Statistical aspects of composite strength. Fatigue and time-dependent deformation.

ME 555.name: Cellular Biomechanics
ME 555.description: Fundamental concepts and experimental techniques in molecular biology, statistical mechanics of polymers, review of solid and fluid mechanics. Mechanics of cellular polymers. Polymer networks and cytoskeleton. The role of stress in cytoskeleton dynamics as related to cell growth, spreading, motility and adhesion. Cellular mechanotransduction. Current research topics in cellular biomechanics.

ME 556.name: Advanced Manufacturing
ME 556.description: A brief overview and evaluation of advanced manufacturing processes and their comparison to traditional manufacturing processes. Classification of advanced manufacturing processes according to the energy used in material removal. Overview of process principles, equipment, machining parameters, process capabilities, and applications.

ME 557.name: Metal Cutting Principles
ME 557.description: The basic principles of metal cutting. The mechanics of metal cutting, heat generation during metal cutting, modern cutting materials, tool life and tool wear, cutting fluids, surface roughness generated by cutting actions, chip control, economics of cutting, chatter vibration, abrasive machining and non-conventional machining processes.

ME 558.name: Impact Mechanics
ME 558.description: Stereomechanical impact. Stress waves in solids. Elementary stress wave theory. Applications of elementary one dimensional stress wave theory. Momentum traps. Spalling in bars and flat plates. Fracture with stress waves in bars.

ME 564.name: Topics in Modern Dynamics
ME 564.description: Phase Space, Equilibrium and Stability, Geometric Dynamics, Analytical Dynamics, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos, Coupled Oscillators and Synchronization, Neurodynamics, Economic Dynamics: Game Theory, Network Dynamics, Evolutionary Dynamics, Dynamics of Microswimmer Robots, Dynamics of Computer Games: Physics Engine.

ME 565.name: Dynamics
ME 565.description: Kinematics of particles and rigid bodies; dynamics of a particle, systems of particles and rigid bodies; central force fields, orbits and trajectories variable mass systems; Lagrange's equations of motion; Hamilton's Principle; variational methods; and applications to dynamics problems and the fundamentals of gyroscopes.

ME 570.name: Dynamics of Aerospace Vehicles
ME 570.description: Introduction to basic aerospace engineering. Introduction to flight and basic aerodynamics. Reference frames and coordinate systems. Frame rotations and Euler angles. Aerospace dynamics: translational and rotational equations of motion. Longitudinal dynamics. Lateral dynamics. Discussion of static stability, trim and dynamic stability. Approximate and linear equations of motion. Basic longitudinal and lateral controls.

ME 571.name: Advanced System Modeling
ME 571.description: Modeling of linear and nonlinear dynamical systems that have components from mechanical, electrical, chemical, thermal and fluidic domains. State space models, interaction between domains, time and frequency domain analysis. Control system design using root locus and bode plots.

ME 574.name: Mobile Robots
ME 574.description: The course is designed as an introductory course on mobile robotics fundamentals. Legged and wheel locomotion will be covered during the lectures with an emphasis on mobile robot kinematics. Kinematic models, mobile robot maneuverability, holonomicity, and motion control of mobile robots will be discussed in detail. Perception in mobile robots will be covered while introducing different sensors and their uses and issues such as sensor uncertainty. Localization of mobile robots will be discussed with a focus on probabilistic techniques. Path planning and obstacle avoidance strategies will be covered.

ME 575.name: Micro/Nano Robotics
ME 575.description: Physics, fabrication, actuation, and sensing for miniature robotic systems, such as mobile robots and micro/nano manipulation devices. An overview of the current state of the micro/nano robotics field, including fabrication methods, small-scale actuators, and sensors. Case studies of various miniature robots and micro/nano systems. Theory behind small-scale robots addressing scaling laws and unique scale-dependent phenomena.

ME 578.name: Vehicle Control Systems
ME 578.description: Design and analysis of vehicle control systems such as cruise control, traction control, active suspensions and advanced vehicle control systems for Intelligent Vehicle-Highway Systems (IVHS). Human factor considerations such as driver interfaces. Fuel Cell and Hybrid Electric Vehicle Control Systems.

ME 579.name: Adaptive Control Systems
ME 579.description: Control systems with undetermined or time-varying parameters, theory and application of self-tuning and model reference adaptive control for continuous and discrete-time deterministic systems, methods for estimation and control, stability of nonlinear systems, adaptation laws, and design and application of adaptive control systems.

ME 580.name: Introduction to MEMS and Micro Systems
ME 580.description: Analysis of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), design of microsystems, components of MEMS devices such as beams, folded suspensions and their analysis & design metrics, beams as micromechanical springs, clean room fabrication techniques, MEMS sensors, accelerometers, gyroscopes, resonant mass/force sensors, MEMS actuation methods, measurement and noise analysis of MEMS devices.

ME 582.name: Fundamentals of Design for Reliability
ME 582.description: Comprehensive definition of reliability. Introduction to reliability engineering, its basic definitions, applications and benefits. Confidence intervals and levels. Concept of target reliability. Case histories from aerospace, military, process control and power systems applications. Basic statistical and analytical functions and distribution types used by reliability engineers. Reliability analysis during the design phase. Qualification tests for components and assemblies. Interfaces of reliability, maintainability and risk engineering. Design guidelines for reliability, maintainability and quality. Statistical reliability testing. Reliability during the production phase. Standards about aerospace, defense and nuclear engineering. System reviews and related checklists. Construction of fault trees and fault tree analysis. Design of reliability testing. Failure causes and types. Effects of environmental conditions, age, mission time and stress. Mission profile and requirements. Failure modes, effects and criticality analysis and two different methods supported by examples. Ageing testing methods. Role of reliability departments in engineering organizations and systems projects.

ME 588.name: Systems Engineering and Product Development
ME 588.description: An introductory understanding of Development Stages for atypical product development cycle. Basic System Engineering Techniques and Approaches. Concepts such as reliability, maintainability, supportability, usability, manufacturability and affordability. Codes and Standards. Technical Data Package and Configuration Management. Test Planning. Mass Affordability Production. Risk Assessment Techniques.

ME 590.name: Mechanical Engineering Seminar
ME 590.description: Participation in university-wide departmental research seminars. Discussion of scientific and technological aspects with supervising faculty.

ME 599.name: Master's Thesis
ME 599.description: A thesis course which complements the requirements towards a MS degree.

ME 615.name: Microfluidics
ME 615.description: Pressure-driven and electrokinetically-driven flows in microchannels, surface effects, micro-fabrication methods, micro/nanoparticles for biotechnology, biochemical reactions and assays, mixing and separation, two-phase flows, integration and design of microfluidic chips.

ME 630.name: Advanced Heat Transfer
ME 630.description: A comprehensive study of conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer in engineering systems. Conduction topics include multidimensional steady and transient analysis, finned surfaces, and shape factors. Convection covers boundary layers, internal and external flows, and developing flow in ducts for both laminar and turbulent regimes. Radiation topics include fundamental laws, directional and spectral property variations, view factors, and radiative exchange between surfaces.

ME 631.name: Conductive Heat Transfer
ME 631.description: Focuses on exact (separation of variables, integral transform techniques and Green's function method) and approximate analytical methods (integral method and variational formulation) to solve problems of conduction heat transfer. Covered topics include heat conduction in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates at steady state as well as the transient processes, steady periodic problems, Duhamel's theorem, heat conduction through composite medium, heat conduction with a moving heat source.

ME 657.name: Nano/Micro Manufacturing
ME 657.description: Lithography, laser processes, mechanical micro-manufacturing, measurement techniques, micro-electrochemical machining, e-beam lithography and ion-beam machining, micro-stereolithography techniques, soft lithography, nanofabrication, nanoimprinting, clean room processes.

ME 690.name: Mechanical Engineering Seminar
ME 690.description: Participation in university-wide departmental research seminars. Discussion of scientific and technological aspects with supervising faculty.

ME 699.name: Ph.D. Dissertation
ME 699.description: A thesis course which complements the requirements towards a PhD degree.
